# Prime Intellect (RL pilot)

The pilot chapter for post-training and RL. Prime Intellect's INTELLECT-2 and INTELLECT-3
reports are unusually explicit that their recipe sections describe "the ablation experiments that
led to it", and both document abandoned paths. That makes them a good test of whether the
experiments-to-final-run template works when the "experiments" are RL ablations on small proxy
models and the "final run" is a released post-trained model. Working notes with sources are in
`data/notes/prime-intellect.md`; the three technical reports were read in full.

```{python}
#| echo: false
from src.chapter import *  # noqa
```

## What the template can and cannot do here

Two things break relative to pretraining. First, there is no compute axis: neither report gives
GPU-hours, cluster size for INTELLECT-2, or the compute of any ablation, so every RL step count
in the data is read off a figure. Second, there is no fitted scaling relation to test: Prime
Intellect's evidence is that findings on 1.5B, 4B and 7B proxies transfer qualitatively to 32B
and 106B, and that benchmark-vs-step curves for INTELLECT-3 showed "no sign of plateauing".
What the record does give is a clean **experiment ladder**: which ablation, at what size,
licensed which decision in the main run.

## The RL experiment ladder

```{python}
e = load.experiments("prime-intellect")
ladder = e[e["stage"] == "post-training/RL"][["project", "intervention", "model_sizes", "metric", "raw_data_available", "source_url"]].copy()
ladder["source_url"] = ladder["source_url"].map(lambda u: f"[src]({u})" if u else "")
display(ladder.reset_index(drop=True))
```

Reading the INTELLECT-2 ladder in order: an async-delay ablation at 1.5B licensed two-step
asynchrony; a difficulty-filtering ablation at 7B (reward 0.34 to 0.42 over about 700 steps once
problems outside a 12.5 to 50 percent pass@8 band were dropped) licensed the 7B model as a
pre-filter for the 285k-task dataset; gradient-norm and entropy-collapse behaviour at 32B led to
two-sided clipping and aggressive gradient clipping (adopted), a larger KL weight (rejected as
too slow) and disabling torch.compile (adopted). The length reward that worked at 1.5B and 7B
did not converge at 32B in the 200 to 350 step main runs and was left unresolved.

INTELLECT-3 added a proxy-model stage: a 4B model validated each new environment and annotated
problem difficulty before anything ran at 106B, and algorithms were ablated under deliberately
high off-policyness (GSPO collapsed, CISPO climbed from 0.3 to 0.8 over about 400 steps).

## Final run against its base

The RL analogue of the final-run star is the released model's score against the base it started
from. INTELLECT-2 started from an already heavily RL-trained base (QwQ-32B) and moved little;
INTELLECT-3 started from a base model (GLM-4.5-Air-Base) and moved a lot.

```{python}
c = load.claims("prime-intellect")
def pairs(project):
    out = []
    for _, r in c[(c["project"] == project) & c["value"].str.contains(" vs ")].iterrows():
        new, base = [float(x) for x in r["value"].split(" vs ")]
        out.append((r["claim"].split(":")[0], base, new))
    return out
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4)); plots.paired_deltas(pairs("intellect-2"), "QwQ-32B (base)", "INTELLECT-2", ax=ax); plt.show()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4)); plots.paired_deltas(pairs("intellect-3"), "GLM-4.5-Air", "INTELLECT-3", ax=ax); plt.show()
```

## Narrative

**Lab shape.** Three flagship runs about six months apart, moving from donated decentralised
compute (INTELLECT-1: up to 112 H100s from 30 contributors over 42 days) to a trusted training
cluster plus a permissionless inference swarm (INTELLECT-2: all runs "over the duration of two
weeks") to a centralised 512-H200 cluster (INTELLECT-3: SFT and RL "including multiple ablations
over the course of two months"). Author counts grew from 12 to 13 to 22.

**Compute that is not published.** INTELLECT-2's training-cluster size, GPU-hours and cost;
the number of ablation runs for either RL project; any development-vs-final split. The derived
figures in the data (about 1.2e5 H200-hours for the INTELLECT-3 RL run, up to about 7.5e5 for
the whole two-month programme) come from node counts, step times and step counts, with the
method in each row. The report does state one compute ratio: inference to training FLOPs of
about 4.5 to 1 in decentralised RL.

**Implication for the template.** For RL labs the reconstructable object is the ladder of
decisions, not a curve. The chapter template should carry a decision-ladder table as a standard
section for Part II, and treat reward-vs-step figures as `figure_only` evidence unless a lab
publishes W&B exports (Prime Intellect's are private).
